mark_codes.C: covered: the existing trait already does this job (a real miss of M3's retrieval)
mark_codes.N: new: the candidate is a different trait (the lexical link is a coincidence)
mark_codes.?: unsure, or the gloss misreads the word

rows.label: lewd
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe coarse, vulgar speech, but lewd is specifically sexual obscenity while crude covers general coarseness and rough humor without being sexual.
rows.opus_reason: Lewd is crude, vulgar speech narrowed to sexual matters, so it is a more specific form of the general coarseness that crude describes.

rows.label: useful
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe working effectively to meet the other person's real needs and solve their problem; 'helpful' adds care for outcomes and going beyond the minimum, a slight difference in emphasis and scope.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe genuinely working to meet what the person needs. Helpful adds caring about outcomes and going beyond the minimum, while useful stresses staying aimed at real needs rather than appearing to engage, so they differ mainly in emphasis.

rows.label: meddling
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve prying into others' private affairs; meddling adds inserting oneself into decisions, while nosy emphasizes curiosity and entitlement to know, so they overlap heavily but each has a distinct element.
rows.opus_reason: Both centre on prying into others' private affairs; meddling goes further by also interfering in their decisions, so it is a broader version of the same concept.

rows.label: unrefined
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe coarse, crude, boisterous behavior that disregards refined manners; 'unladylike' is the same quality framed around genteel expectations for women, so it differs mainly in scope and emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Unladylike is the same coarse, crude manners as unrefined, narrowed to flouting genteel expectations for women and adding boisterousness.

rows.label: tepid
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe low energy and lack of investment, but apathetic goes further into outright not caring and minimal effort, while tepid is a mild lukewarm manner; same core with a difference in degree.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe a lack of investment and enthusiasm. Apathetic carries the same lukewarm disengagement further, into not caring at all and minimal effort.

rows.label: raunchy
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve coarse, vulgar talk and crude jokes, but raunchy is specifically sexually explicit while crude is general vulgarity with no sexual focus, so each can occur without the other.
rows.opus_reason: Raunchy is crude, coarse talk narrowed to sexual explicitness, so it is the same vulgarity with a narrower sexual focus.

rows.label: manipulable
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe readily yielding opinions and choices to others' pressure with little firm position of one's own; the differences are minor emphasis (flattery vs. forceful speakers, loyalties).
rows.opus_reason: Both describe readily yielding one's opinions and choices to others' pressure without firm resistance, essentially the same concept with slight emphasis differences.

rows.label: uninterested
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a lack of interest or concern in the matter and the people involved; apathetic adds a minimal-effort emphasis while uninterested stresses flat, detached manner and no curiosity.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe a lack of interest and concern for the matter, the people, and the outcome; apathetic adds minimal effort while uninterested stresses absent curiosity, a difference of emphasis.

rows.label: dwindling
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a persona living with gradually failing strength and energy and talking about it; they differ only slightly in emphasis (plain speech and month-by-month slipping versus needing help over years and frequent talk of limits).
rows.opus_reason: Both describe gradual loss of bodily strength, with tiring and frank talk of what the body can no longer do. They differ only slightly in pace and in the emphasis on needing help.

rows.label: purposeful
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe keeping actions aimed at clear goals with definite intent; purposeful adds steady determination, but the core concept is essentially the same.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe acting with a clear aim, each step directed toward a chosen goal; purposeful adds a little emphasis on steady determination, but the concept is the same.

rows.label: racy
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve sexually charged speech, but racy is playfully suggestive and bawdy while obscene is crudely offensive and shocking, so obscene is a stronger, more offensive version with a different tone.
rows.opus_reason: Both are sexual talk, but obscene is a cruder, offensive extreme of racy's playful suggestiveness, a difference of degree and tone.

rows.label: lovable
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe an endearing, warm charm that draws fondness from others, with adorable being nearly the same concept as lovable and perhaps slightly more about cuteness, while lovable here also stresses putting people at ease.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe an endearing, warm charm that draws fondness from others. Adorable even defines itself as lovable, so the two labels are effectively interchangeable.

rows.label: mocking
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe scornfully ridiculing others' ideas, efforts and failings, so the concepts are nearly interchangeable, with only slight differences in emphasis.

rows.label: matter of fact
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe plain, unembellished expression, but prosaic focuses on the absence of imagery and beauty, while matter-of-fact stresses directness, practicality and lack of sentiment.
rows.opus_reason: Prosaic is a matter-of-fact plainness of expression that stresses the absence of imagery or beauty, so it is essentially the target with a narrower aesthetic emphasis.

rows.label: uncouth
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe coarse, unrefined behavior with no concern for polish, but 'crude' centers on vulgar speech and humor while 'uncouth' covers rough manners more broadly (e.g., eating noisily).
rows.opus_reason: Both describe coarse, unrefined behavior. Uncouth covers manners broadly, while crude stresses vulgar language and humor; the two largely overlap and differ mainly in emphasis.

rows.label: jeering
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe mocking others with scorn and ridicule; jeering emphasizes active taunting and sneering remarks, while derisive is a slightly broader attitude of scorn, so they differ only in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both mean scornfully mocking others and treating their failings as things to ridicule; jeering only adds an emphasis on vocal taunts.

rows.label: vulgar
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve crude, offensive speech, but vulgar is a broader habitual coarseness including rough manners, while obscene is specifically lewd and sexual language meant to shock; each can occur without the other.
rows.opus_reason: Obscene is a narrower, sexually focused form of the crude, coarse speech that vulgar covers more broadly, rough manners included.

rows.label: waning
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe progressive loss of physical strength and measuring life by what the body can no longer do; 'declining' adds a longer timescale and needing help, with only slightly different emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe gradual physical decline and loss of bodily capacity, differing only slightly in timescale (weekly vs. yearly) and emphasis.

rows.label: raunchy
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe crude, sexually explicit speech; obscene stresses offensiveness and shock, raunchy stresses bawdy humor and unapologetic bluntness, so they are close but differ in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe crude, sexually explicit speech. Obscene is the same quality pushed further, toward language that offends and disgusts listeners.

rows.label: unfeminine
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a woman whose rough, unpolished manner flouts conventional gentleness expectations; unladylike adds boisterousness, crude jokes and flaunting, while unfeminine stresses bluntness and lack of delicacy.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe rough, unpolished manners that defy conventional expectations of women. Unladylike carries this further into loud, crude, boisterous rudeness.

rows.label: rumpled
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe an habitually untidy appearance with indifference to how one looks to others, and the descriptions are nearly identical in meaning.

rows.label: crass
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve crude, tasteless speech, but crass is general coarse insensitivity while obscene is specifically sexual lewdness; each can occur without the other.
rows.opus_reason: Obscene is a narrower, sexually focused form of the same coarse, tasteless vulgarity that crass describes more broadly across speech and behaviour.

rows.label: lewd
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe habitually crude, sexually offensive speech; obscene adds an emphasis on shocking or disgusting listeners, but the core concept is the same.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe habitually speaking in sexually crude, offensive language; obscene adds only a slight emphasis on shocking listeners.

rows.label: good-hearted
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a kind, caring disposition toward others, but benevolent stresses promoting wellbeing and ethical concern while good-hearted stresses warm, freely given generosity, so they are near-synonyms differing in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe kindly goodwill toward others. Benevolent leans toward actively promoting everyone's wellbeing on ethical grounds, while good-hearted stresses a warm, freely generous disposition, so they differ only in emphasis.

rows.label: untoward
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve breaking propriety, but unladylike is a narrower kind of impropriety (coarse, boisterous, rough manners against genteel expectations for women), while untoward covers any improper or unseemly conduct.
rows.opus_reason: Unladylike is a narrower, gender-specific form of the same impropriety: coarse conduct that breaks genteel norms. Untoward covers improper, unseemly behaviour in general.

rows.label: unpolished
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe coarse, rough speech and manners with no concern for refinement; 'crude' leans more toward vulgar language and humor, while 'unpolished' also covers bluntness and general conduct.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe coarse, unrefined speech and manners with no concern for polish; crude leans more toward vulgar humor, unpolished toward general lack of refinement.

rows.label: snoopy
rows.sonnet_reason: Both mean prying into others' private affairs; 'nosy' adds a sense of entitlement but is essentially the same concept and interchangeable.

rows.label: sullen
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe silent, resentful brooding with curt answers instead of voicing the grievance; sulky is tied to a specific slight and lingering resentment, but the core is essentially the same.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe silent, withdrawn resentment with clipped replies; sulky adds only the slight as trigger and lingering after resolution, a minor difference of emphasis.

rows.label: sullen
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a silent, brooding, withdrawn mood with curt grudging replies; morose is a bit more about gloomy dourness, sullen more about resentful displeasure, so they differ slightly in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe a withdrawn, silent bad mood with grudging, curt replies; sullen stresses bottled resentment, while morose stresses general gloomy dourness.

rows.label: derogatory
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe habitually belittling and demeaning others through speech; 'insulting' stresses cutting remarks to the listener while 'derogatory' also includes contemptuous manner and running down character, a minor difference in emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe habitually belittling and demeaning others with contemptuous speech, so either label could stand in for the other.

rows.label: crude
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve vulgar speech, but obscene is specifically sexual and shocking, while crude is broader coarseness and lack of refinement; obscene is a narrower, more intense subset.
rows.opus_reason: Obscene is a narrower, more extreme form of crude speech, focused on sexual lewdness meant to shock, while crude covers coarse vulgarity in general.

rows.label: smutty
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve crude sexual talk and innuendo, but smutty stresses a habit of steering ordinary talk toward bawdy jokes and double meanings, while obscene stresses offensive, shocking lewdness, so each adds something the other lacks.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe crude sexual talk and innuendo; obscene is the same quality pushed further, toward language that shocks or offends, while smutty stresses steering conversation toward sex.

rows.label: sombre
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a habitually heavy, gloomy outlook that dwells on negatives; melancholic stresses sadness and brooding, while sombre stresses a muted, serious demeanor, so they are near-synonyms with slightly different emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe a habitually low mood with a focus on the negative; sombre stresses a muted, grave outward manner, while melancholic stresses inner sadness and brooding.

rows.label: fake
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe putting on a false front and presenting a self one doesn't actually hold; 'phony' is nearly synonymous with 'fake', only slightly more specific about the feigned warmth, interest, or expertise.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe presenting a false self and feigning sincerity or feelings one lacks; the labels are interchangeable.

rows.label: sneering
rows.sonnet_reason: Both express scornful contempt toward others, but sneering is a settled attitude of looking down shown in tone and manner, while derisive centers on active mockery and ridicule of ideas and efforts, so they overlap without being the same.
rows.opus_reason: Both are open scorn toward others; derisive puts the emphasis on mocking ridicule, while sneering stresses contemptuous looking-down, a difference of emphasis within the same concept.

rows.label: moldable
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe readily yielding one's opinions to others' pressure; malleable adds plans and loyalties but is essentially the same concept.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe yielding to others' pressure and reshaping one's opinions. Malleable also covers plans and loyalties, which only broadens the same concept slightly.

rows.label: scornful
rows.sonnet_reason: Both involve contemptuous disdain toward others, but scornful is looking down and showing disdain in general, while derisive specifically adds active mockery and ridicule; each can occur without the other.
rows.opus_reason: Derisive is scorn expressed specifically through mockery and ridicule, a narrower, more active form of the same disdain that scornful describes.

rows.label: crude
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe coarse, vulgar speech, crude jokes and rough manners with no concern for refinement; 'unladylike' is the same quality framed by gendered genteel expectations and adds boisterousness.
rows.opus_reason: Unladylike is crude coarseness of speech and manner framed against genteel expectations for women, adding boisterousness and a gendered norm-flouting scope.

rows.label: artificial
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe staged, insincere warmth presented as genuine; phony is slightly broader, covering faked expertise and a false self, while artificial stresses a forced, affected manner.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe a staged, insincere show of warmth. Phony is broader, also covering faked expertise and a false self, while artificial centres on an affected manner.

rows.label: fading
rows.sonnet_reason: Both describe a persona whose health and strength are gradually failing, with tiring easily and trouble with ordinary tasks; declining stresses a longer span and more need for help, so they differ mainly in degree and emphasis.
rows.opus_reason: Both describe gradual loss of bodily strength and tiring easily, differing only in timescale (months vs years) and in emphasis on needing help.
